<description>
The `partially_signed_transaction_deserialize` target feeds raw bytes to the PSBT parser. Byte-level mutations rarely produce well-formed key-value maps with valid keydata (pubkeys, xpubs, control blocks, DER signatures, etc), so most inputs are rejected early and the deeper per-field parsing is rarely reached.

This PR adds a custom mutator for PSBT which is ported from bitcoinfuzz (with some changes).  The mutator splits the input into global/input/output maps of key-value records, applies the mutations and serializes the result again. The first commit is a preparation to allow targets to provide a custom mutator by adding an optional `mutator` field to
`FuzzTargetOptions`.

note: LLM assisted on porting the custom mutator.
</description>

<commits>
3eb682fadb fuzz: allow targets to provide a libFuzzer custom mutator

Add an optional `mutator` field to FuzzTargetOptions. When the fuzz
binary is linked against libFuzzer, LLVMFuzzerCustomMutator dispatches
to the selected target's mutator, falling back to LLVMFuzzerMutate for
targets that don't set one.

Custom mutators can call FuzzDefaultMutate() to apply libFuzzer's
default mutations to parts of the input.

libFuzzer disables -len_control by default whenever
LLVMFuzzerCustomMutator is linked in, which would otherwise affect every
target. Targets without a custom mutator get -len_control=100 restored,
unless it was set explicitly.

Whether the engine provides LLVMFuzzerMutate is detected at configure
time, so builds using other engines or the built-in main are unaffected.

f34b7ff64f fuzz: add structure-aware PSBT mutator

Add a custom mutator for raw PSBTs, ported from bitcoinfuzz, and use it
for the partially_signed_transaction_deserialize target.
</commits>
